contentHtml:
Beginning in Pune with an initial investment of Rs 2,000–2,500 crore, it aims to be present across more than 10 cities within the next 15 years

Bajaj Integrated Health System (BIHS), the healthcare venture backed by the Bajaj Group, has unveiled Nivara, marking a new chapter in the Group’s legacy, with a long-term vision to shape a more connected healthcare ecosystem across India.

Beginning in Pune with an initial investment of Rs 2,000–2,500 crore, BIHS aims to be present across more than 10 cities within the next 15 years.

Derived from Sanskrit, ‘Nivara’ signifies safety, protection and comfort. Under Nivara, BIHS will establish an integrated healthcare network, rolled out across three formats – Medical Centres, Ambulatory Centres and Hospitals over the next few years. The network will integrate consultations, diagnostics, pharmacy, physiotherapy and homecare services, with plans to subsequently expand into hospital-based care. Nivara’s model is designed to shift healthcare from episodic treatment towards continuous health management, supporting patients from prevention and early diagnosis through treatment, recovery and long-term care.

At Nivara, ‘Together in Health & Care’ reflects the importance of bringing people, medical expertise and healthcare services together to support patients through every stage of their health journey.

Nirav Bajaj, Managing Director & CEO, BIHS, said, “For over a century, the Bajaj Group has built institutions founded on trust, responsibility and a long-term commitment to India’s progress. With Nivara, we are bringing that same approach to healthcare. Our ambition is to build a trusted healthcare institution that delivers better patient outcomes, greater transparency and a more accountable care experience. We are proud to begin this journey in Pune, a city that has been closely associated with the Bajaj Group for generations.”

Nivara seeks to address a broader range of healthcare needs beyond hospital settings, bringing greater focus to preventive care, early diagnosis, chronic disease management and outpatient services.

“Healthcare journeys are often fragmented, with patients navigating multiple providers, facilities and care settings with limited coordination between them. At Nivara, we have designed our model to create greater continuity across the care journey, supported by clinical standards, shared governance frameworks and a connected technology backbone. Our focus is on enabling coordinated care while maintaining consistency in quality, safety and patient experience,” said Devina Kartha, Chief Enterprise & Governance Officer, BIHS.

The Nivara ecosystem follows a primary-care-first approach, placing patients and their healthcare needs at the centre. It focuses on addressing patient needs across the health journey, spanning prevention, early diagnosis, treatment, recovery, and long-term health management. Technology serves as an enabler, supporting care teams with access to relevant clinical information, advanced clinical tools, and outcomes monitoring to facilitate informed decision-making and continuous improvement in patient care.
